name: Barbados
headline: Barbados: +2.7% growth in 2025, 0.9% inflation, debt 96% of GDP
sections: Barbados is a $7.9 billion economy (2025), the world's 161st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.7% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $26K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 4.9% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 0.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 7.2% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 18.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 96% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 130% in 2020. The general government balance is −0.2% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −5.9% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Net FDI inflows were 3.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 73% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.3 years (2024). Population: 292 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
